hints: A root-to-node path query is the sum of values along that path.
Flatten nodes by DFS order and store each node's value in a Fenwick tree.
For each node, add its value at entry and its negation just after its subtree; a prefix at tin[u] then equals the root path sum.
analogy: A node's value is active in the Euler array from its entry through the end of its subtree.
example: If root=5, parent value=2, and node value=3, the prefix at its entry gives path sum 10.
algorithm: On entry at tin[u], add value[u]; at tout[u]+1 add -value[u]. Point updates change both markers; query prefix(tin[u]) for root-to-u total.
correctness: The entry/exit difference markers include exactly the ancestors of u at its entry position, so their prefix sum is the desired path sum.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time and O(n) space.
